question.text: In computing data for performance benchmarking, SEBI's operational guidelines specify the basis of reporting for Cat III AIF returns. Which of the following is correct?

answer.text: Post-tax NAV; AUM equals committed capital
Pre-tax NAV; AUM equals value of total capital drawn down under the scheme
Post-expense, post-carry, post-tax NAV; AUM equals NAV of the scheme
Gross-of-fees NAV; AUM equals Gross Asset Value including leverage

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI operational guidelines (Box 8.6, Section A, para (f) and (g)): 'AUM for the purpose of reporting and benchmarking shall be the value of total capital drawn down under the Scheme. Performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on pre-tax Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Scheme.' For Cat III benchmarks specifically, returns are post-expense, pre-carry, pre-tax. **The Trap:** Option A swaps the rules (post-tax and committed). Option C adds carry post-deduction and post-tax — inconsistent with SEBI. Option D uses GAV, which overstates due to leverage for a Cat III fund (up to 2x leverage cap). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C and XIX-D test the same pre-tax/drawn-capital convention. This is a common trap in XIX-B (Distributor) exams where candidates confuse NAV bases. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III fund taxed at fund-level MMR, the pre-tax vs post-tax gap is large (MMR ~42.74%) — always clarify in your investor letter whether the reported return is pre-tax (as submitted to the benchmarking agency) or post-tax (what the investor actually keeps). Mixing these up invites LP complaints and potential mis-selling claims.
